narratives.Overview:
# Next-build (bound recut)

Filed Wanted 1 reuse of #1378 fields is REJECTED. Dispatch-cohort consent and close-unit consent stay distinct. `cohort_vbriefs` is the dispatch set, not a close grant. `--allow-close` is not one-PR-unit consent. Do not parse an implement list or free-form issue/comment text as the mint. Cite `evidenceSatisfiesImplementationApproval`.

Keep one-PR batching. Make it explicit. Default without a one-PR-unit grant: one origin → one PR.

The gitignored `.deft/one-pr-unit/` disk store is NOT the verifier-visible record.

## Bound remedy (lean 5658220623)

1. Distinct one-PR-unit identity. Do not reuse #1378 `allocation_plan_id` / `batching_rationale` / `operator_approval_evidence`, `--allow-close`, or an implement list. Cite `evidenceSatisfiesImplementationApproval`.
2. Mint UX: keep `deft authz:grant` / `refuseNonInteractiveMint`. The mint calls the App. Opaque grant id is not a bearer credential. Only the App store plus the bound PR node id authorizes.
3. Canonical store: Directive GitHub App private transactional store. Unique active-membership on every normalized `(repo, issue-id)`. One transaction reserves the whole exact set or the mint fails. Overlapping concurrent mints abort. Check-runs are a projection, not the store. Do not keep `.deft/one-pr-unit` as SoT.
4. PR-unit bind: at mint the claim is `reserved` and unbound. It binds irreversibly to the GitHub PR node id on first App interaction. A later presentation from a different node id is refused.
5. Worker identity: dest-placed workers receive a Directive App installation token whose requested permissions are an explicit allowlist: `contents: write`, `issues: none`. Verify the permissions GitHub returns. Omit of the `permissions` object is refuse. Worker context has no operator `gh` store, no App private key, no Pull requests write, no Checks write, no Administration, no ruleset-bypass identity. Local PreToolUse / `.deft-directive-disable` are not that host.
6. Merge lane: GitHub merge queue. On every `merge_group.checks_requested`, the App resolves every constituent PR, reads live `closingIssuesReferences`, PR-body declarations, and commit-message declarations, applies the explicit grammar (not `CLOSING_KEYWORD_RE`), compares each PR unit to its bound reservation, and reports the App-restricted required check on that merge-group SHA. Missing constituent, unreadable source, unbound claim, extra declaration, or set mismatch is non-passing. Single-origin / no-grant PRs still get an App-posted passing check. Literal "dequeue" is not an event name.
7. Automated close only through the App after consume. Invert fail-open close classifier for close-shaped ops. No `DEFT_ALLOW_*` escape. `restCloseIssue` / umbrella reconcile must present claimed set.
8. UI/raw API closes are recovery-class (`closed_by` ≠ App), not prevention. Webhook reopen is recovery.
9. Consumption states: reserved (unbound) → bound → member-complete* → spent | revoked | expired. Expiry 24 hours from mint. Revoker: minting operator via human-presence mint. PR closed unmerged revokes.
10. Direct default-branch commits that close origins still need an App reservation; `allowDirectCommitsToMaster` does not bypass. Commit-message Closes without the merge-group check is recovery-class.
11. Implement-class `solo` with `|cohort_vbriefs| > 1` and no grant is a config error. Overlap serializes. The four named sources are not close-permission.
12. Docs: on `swarm:readiness` failure / Phase 0 exit, print serialize-N-PRs. Close-surface docs next to github.md. PR-template prose is docs, not the gate. Live Greptile-only ruleset is an implementation gap, not a contradiction.

Citing lean 5658220623 and synthesis 5658223755 (table 5658221934).
